messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2.5 °C**.  

This is a consequence of the negative volume change when ice forms (solid water occupies less volume than liquid water). As the pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, the equilibrium temperature at which ice and liquid coexist shifts to lower temperatures. At the triple‑point pressure (~0.61 kPa) the freezing point is only about +0.01 °C; at 10 kPa it is about –2.5 °C.
